rows.observation: Federal Funds Rate at 3.88% (effective, Oct 2), up 13 bps from prior month (3.75%), above 3-mo MA (3.67%) and 12-mo MA (3.71%). First hike cycle in >3 years underway.

Fed Balance Sheet roughly stable: Total assets $6.743T (Sep 30), -$4.7B m/m; Reserve balances $2.948T, +$17.9B w/w. Reverse repo usage collapsed to $1B (Oct 5) from $1.5B prior day, vs 6-mo avg $2.6B and 12-mo avg $3.5B — liquidity draining from facility.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack (2026 voter) turned explicitly hawkish at NABE (Oct 12): prefers 'smaller adjustments relatively quickly' to anchor inflation expectations; says policy not restrictive enough; neutral rate 'may be higher, but hard to determine'; argues rate hikes unlikely to address main inflation drivers (tariffs, AI infrastructure demand). Stopped short of backing October hike.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller: Surging long-term yields reflect strong growth and AI investment boom, not unanchored inflation expectations. Estimates diminished safe-haven premium adding 50–70 bps to yields (unverified). Expects AI capex cycle to continue 2–3 years. Still sees inflation 'too high'; further hikes possible if data warrant.

September FOMC Minutes (released Oct 7): Most participants judged further tightening before year-end 'may be appropriate'; majority saw at least one more hike in 2026. Unanimous 25 bp hike to 3.75–4.00% on Sep 16.
Market pricing: October hike odds ~19–22% (down from 64% late Sep); December hike fully priced; ~75–80 bps total tightening priced by end-2027. Fed blackout begins Oct 17 ahead of Oct 27–28 meeting.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh: Ended forward guidance; declined to submit dot-plot projections. IMF fireside chat in Bangkok Oct 16 (00:30 ET) — last scheduled Fed speech before blackout.

CPI (Aug, latest): 334.13, +1.32 m/m; Core CPI 337.76, +0.97 m/m. Both above 3-mo and 6-mo MAs. September CPI due Wed Oct 14 — consensus headline +0.5–0.6% m/m (3.6–3.7% y/y), core +0.2% m/m (down from 0.3%).
Core PCE (Jul): 130.46, +0.33 m/m; 3-mo annualized run rate 2.7–2.8% (tracking above target). MNI: core PCE tracking in high 0.20s m/m.
PPI (Aug): 287.93, +2.75 m/m — significant monthly jump, +6.3 vs 6-mo MA, +16.1 vs 12-mo MA. Pipeline pressure elevated.
Breakeven inflation stable: 5-yr 2.36%, 10-yr 2.36% (Oct 5) — little movement despite oil volatility. 1-yr breakeven ~2.90%, 5-yr ~2.41% (per market sources).
University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (Aug): 51.7, -3.5 m/m. Current conditions index at record low 44.7; 1-yr inflation expectations 4.7% (highest since May).
Energy: WTI ~$93, Brent ~$105–106 (Oct 12–13). Iran war, Hormuz disruptions, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia keeping risk premium elevated. G7 to release 100M barrels from SPR.

September Payrolls: +29K (Oct 2 release) vs ~90K consensus — weakest print in months. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. Downward revisions: Jul -10K (was +21K), Aug 133K (was 162K) — combined -60K.
Average Hourly Earnings: +0.1% m/m (vs 0.3% exp), +3.0% y/y — slowest since May 2021. Real wages negative vs 3.4% headline inflation.
Job Openings (Aug): 7.079M, -256K m/m — notable decline, below 3-mo MA (7.351M). Quits/Layoffs data pending.
Initial Jobless Claims (w/e Sep 26): 197K — low, below 30-day MA (203K). ADP private payrolls (4-wk avg) 24.75K.
Labor Force Participation: 61.8% (Sep), +0.2 pp m/m. Household survey showed employment +406K, labor force +485K — mixed signal vs payroll weakness.
Real GDP Growth (Q2): 2.2% annualized (down from 2.5% Q1). Atlanta Fed GDPNow Q3 tracking 3.6% (down from 5%+ in July).
Retail Sales (Aug): $737.8B, +$8.2B m/m — but prior month's +1.2% largely fuel-driven; real spending may be flatter.
Personal Income (Aug): $27.627T, +$66.6B m/m. PCE $22.309T, +$190.8B m/m.
Industrial Production (Aug): 103.07, essentially flat m/m (+0.02).

Housing: 30-yr mortgage 7.28% (Oct 1), +25 bps w/w, +58 bps vs 30-day MA (6.69%). Freddie Mac 30-yr hit 7.4% Oct 8. Redfin: pending home sales -4% m/m Sep (lowest since 2014), all 50 metros down; active listings highest since Mar 2020; contract cancellation rate 14.5% (record). Building permits -30K, starts -34K, existing sales -80K. Home Price Index still rising (+0.4 m/m Jul).
Yield Curve Bear Steepening: 2-yr 4.83% (+5 bps w/w), 5-yr 5.06% (+5 bps), 10-yr 5.28% (+4 bps), 30-yr ~5.55%. Real 10-yr 2.92% (+4 bps). Yields at multi-decade highs; long end leading.
US Treasury doubling debt buyback program to provide liquidity to long-end as 10/20/30-yr yields hit multi-decade highs.
Credit Spreads Narrowing: HY OAS 3.10% (-14 bps), IG OAS 0.85% (-1 bp) — despite higher rates, risk appetite holding.
Equities Near Highs: S&P 500 7,723 (+0.7% Oct 2), NASDAQ 27,191 (+1.2%). VIX 15.31 (-1.08). CNN Fear & Greed 43 (Fear); AAII Bearish 46.5% > Bullish 34.6%.

BlackRock: Cut US equities to neutral (from overweight), upgraded short-dated Treasuries to overweight. Says 160 bps of Fed tightening priced in is 'overdone'; 10-yr yield up 110 bps YTD to ~5.25% creates value at front end.
Dollar Strength: DXY ~102.6 (near yearly high), Broad USD Index 121.38. EUR/USD 1.1150 (17-month low). Driven by hawkish Fed rhetoric + oil/geopolitics.

Iran War / Strait of Hormuz: Ongoing conflict, shipping/insurance costs >1/3 cargo value on some routes. Iran fortifying nuclear sites (Pickaxe Mountain, Natanz), threatening wider retaliation if US strikes resume after Nov midterms. US 3rd carrier group + Marines deploying to region. US-Iran interim Hormuz reopening talks ongoing; Iran reviewing US response.

Trump-Putin Diesel Deal (Oct 9): US temporarily waived sanctions on Russian diesel (300K tonnes Oct, 500K Nov, 1M Dec). Announced 'energy ceasefire' Russia-Ukraine — neither side confirmed; Ukraine says Russia struck 6+ energy facilities since. EU approved largest Russia sanctions expansion (1,569 entities/individuals) Oct 12, pushing back on diesel deal. UK PM accused Iran of plot vs RAF Fairford.
Saudi Arabia under Houthi missile/drone attacks: Riyadh airport closed until Oct 17; air defense investigation underway. At least 18 deaths recent strikes.
US Threatening Ukraine: Per FT/Reuters, US officials warned allies/Ukraine of cutting intelligence sharing and PURL weapons channel if refinery strikes continue.

US-Europe Four-Point Ukraine Peace Proposal (per WashPost): 1) Ukraine reconstruction, 2) Mutual security guarantees (Art 5-style), 3) Energy integration (Russia-EU pipeline, Ukraine transit fees), 4) Ceasefire on current front lines (ceding occupied territory to Russia).
NATO: Gen. Grynkewich (SACEUR) at Warsaw Forum: 'We will block, blunt, break enemy forces' if Russia attacks allies. Russia nuclear threats re Kaliningrad.
IMF: Flags risks to global economy from AI market correction, war, debt. BoJ expected to hike gradually; RBA leaves door open to further hikes.
China: CXMT developing rival server memory — pressuring SK Hynix/Samsung. OpenAI annualized revenue reportedly ~$50B (below $68–70B circulating).

Policy Dilemma: Fed boxed between cooling labor market (weak payrolls, slowing wages) and persistent inflation (core PCE ~3%, core CPI ~2.5%, services sticky). Hammack/Waller favor continued tightening; Williams/Jefferson urge patience.
Long-End Doing Fed's Work: 30-yr mortgage 7.4%, housing freezing, real yields rising — financial conditions tightening without further hikes.

AI Capex vs Inflation: Waller argues AI investment driving real rates up; Hammack says AI demand outside rate tool. Both acknowledge AI adding to specific price pressures (chips, energy, data centers).
Geopolitics → Energy → Inflation → Rates: Iran war, Hormuz, Russia-Ukraine, Trump diesel deal all feeding oil volatility. Oil breakevens not tracking crude — market pricing demand destruction.
Fiscal/Debt: US deficit ~6% GDP; Treasury buybacks expanding; debt service costs rising with yields. Japan/UK/Italy flagged as vulnerable.
2027 Hike Pricing Most Exposed: ~50 bps above Fed path priced for 2027; soft CPI could unwind fastest.
